newsitem.title: UK: UK government plans curbs on knife advertising.
newsitem.headline: UK government plans curbs on knife advertising.

text.p: Home Secretary Michael Howard said on Tuesday he favoured new restrictions on the marketing and advertising of knives to prevent them being sold as aggressive weapons.
Howard said he was willing to help James Wray, an opposition Labour party member of parliament, with a private member's bill to bring in the curbs.
Wray has won first place in the ballot for private members' bills in the current session of parliament, giving him a good chance of getting a bill on the statute book if it has government backing.
In a letter to Labour home affairs spokesman Jack Straw, Howard said: "I...would wish to introduce an offence of marketing a knife in a way which suggests an aggressive use for it."
"This would apply both to the name of the knife and any marketing literature associated with it...This measure would bite particularly upon advertising."
Howard said he also wanted to give the police greater powers to stop and search people they believe to be carrying knives.
